arxiv-2109-11445.title: Critical temperatures of a model cuprate
arxiv-2109-11445.creator: Yu. D. Panov
arxiv-2109-11445.description: Abstract The problem of competing orderings in the high-temperature cuprate materials is widely discussed for the last years. We present the mean-field approximation results for the spin-pseudospin model accounting for the on-site and inter-site correlations, the antiferromagnetic exchange coupling, the one- and two-particle transport.

arxiv-2310-02416.title: Bag of Tricks for Fully Test-Time Adaptation
arxiv-2310-02416.creator: Saypraseuth Mounsaveng, Florent Chiaroni, Malik Boudiaf, Marco Pedersoli, Ismail Ben Ayed ÉTS Montréal, Canada
arxiv-2310-02416.description: Abstract Fully Test-Time Adaptation (TTA), which aims at adapting models to data drifts, has recently attracted wide interest. Numerous tricks and techniques have been proposed to ensure robust learning on arbitrary streams of unlabeled data. However, assessing the true impact of each individual technique and obtaining a fair comparison still constitutes a significant challenge.

arxiv-2404-03499.title: Comprehensible Artificial Intelligence on Knowledge Graphs: A Survey.
arxiv-2404-03499.creator: Simon Schramm, Christoph Wehner, Ute Schmid
arxiv-2404-03499.description: Abstract Artificial Intelligence applications gradually move outside the safe walls of research labs and invade our daily lives. This is also true for Machine Learning methods on Knowledge Graphs, which has led to a steady increase in their application since the beginning of the 21 ​ s ​ t 21st century.

arxiv-2406-11128.title: Model Adaptation for Time Constrained Embodied Control
arxiv-2406-11128.creator: Jaehyun Song, Minjong Yoo, Honguk Woo
arxiv-2406-11128.description: Abstract When adopting a deep learning model for embodied agents, it is required that the model structure be optimized for specific tasks and operational conditions. Such optimization can be static such as model compression or dynamic such as adaptive inference.

arxiv-2410-23762.title: Efficient Performance Analysis of Modular Rewritable Petri Nets
arxiv-2410-23762.creator: Lorenzo Capra, Marco Gribaudo
arxiv-2410-23762.description: Abstract Petri Nets (PN) are extensively used as a robust formalism to model concurrent and distributed systems; however, they encounter difficulties in accurately modeling adaptive systems. To address this issue, we defined rewritable PT nets (RwPT) using Maude , a declarative language that ensures consistent rewriting logic semantics.

pmc-10505155.title: Exploring the effect of pain on response to reward loss in calves
pmc-10505155.creator: Thomas Ede, Marina A. G. von Keyserlingk, Daniel M. Weary
pmc-10505155.description: Negative emotional states are known to interact, potentially aggravating one another. In this study, we used a well validated paradigm (successive negative contrast, SNC) to determine if pain from a common procedure (disbudding) influences responses to a reward downshift. Holstein calves (n = 30) were trained to approach a 0.5 L milk reward.

pmc-10595006.title: The novel immunobiotic Clostridium butyricum S-45-5 displays broad-spectrum antiviral activity in vitro and in vivo by inducing immune modulation
pmc-10595006.creator: Kiramage Chathuranga, Yeseul Shin, Md Bashir Uddin, Jayoung Paek, W. A. Gayan Chathuranga, Yebin Seong, Lu Bai, Hongik Kim, Jeong Hwan Shin, Young-Hyo Chang, Jong-Soo Lee
pmc-10595006.description: Clostridium butyricum is known as a probiotic butyric acid bacterium that can improve the intestinal environment. In this study, we isolated a new strain of C. butyricum from infant feces and evaluated its physiological characteristics and antiviral efficacy by modulating the innate immune responses in vitro and in vivo. The isolated C. butyricum S-45-5 showed typical characteristics of C.

pmc-10735983.title: ASSOCIATIONS BETWEEN GAIT MEASURES AND QUADRICEPS MUSCLE THICKNESS AS MEASURED BY POINT-OF-CARE ULTRASOUND
pmc-10735983.creator: Uyanga Ganbat, Boris Feldman, Shane Arishenkoff, Graydon Meneilly, Kenneth Madden
pmc-10735983.description: Gait parameters and sarcopenia predict falls risk which is one of the major causes of both mortality and morbidity among older adults. Our objective was to evaluate whether anterior thigh muscle measured by point-of-care ultrasound is significantly associated with standard gait measures. All subjects were referred from ambulatory geriatric medicine clinics at an academic center.

pmc-11656094.title: STING Activation in Macrophages and Microglia Drives Poststroke Inflammation: Implications for Neuroinflammatory Mechanisms and Therapeutic Interventions
pmc-11656094.creator: Zhiruo Liu, Qin Qin, Shisi Wang, Xinmei Kang, Yuxin Liu, Lei Wei, Zhengqi Lu, Wei Cai, Mengyan Hu
pmc-11656094.description: BackgroundMonocyte‐derived macrophages and microglia initially adopt an anti‐inflammatory phenotype following stroke but later transition to a pro‐inflammatory state. The mechanisms underlying this phenotypic shift remain unclear. This study investigates the activation dynamics of molecular signaling pathways in macrophages and microglia after stroke.

pmc-12415689.creator: Ngai Sze Wong, Bonnie Chun Kwan Wong, Denise Pui-Chung Chan, Danny King Fai Cheung, Heather Ki Wai To, Sze Long Chung, Margaret Ip, Shui Shan Lee

This study assessed its prevalence, resistance and coinfection with Chlamydia trachomatis/Neisseria gonorrhoeae infections in MSM with HIV.MethodsMSM in HIV care in Hong Kong were recruited during 2023–24 for completion of an online survey, and self-collection of urine specimens, rectal and pharyngeal swabs, which were tested for C. trachomatis, N.

pmc-13069063.title: Influence of structured output constraints on GPT-5-Thinking, Gemini 2.5 Pro, and open-weight LLMs for radiology protocol selection
pmc-13069063.creator: Mohammed Bahaaeldin, Sebastian Nowak, Oleksandra Seidel, Alexander Isaak, Dmitrij Kravchenko, Annemarie Proff, Tatjana Dell, Daniel Kuetting, Julian A Luetkens, Narine Mesropyan
pmc-13069063.description: ObjectiveTo evaluate the impact of constraining proprietary and open large language models (LLMs) to structured outputs in processing radiology request forms (RRF).Materials and methodsWe evaluated five LLMs—two proprietary (GPT-5-Thinking, Gemini 2.5 Pro) and three open (Qwen3-235B-A22B-Thinking, gpt-oss-120b, medgemma-27b-it)—on 100 RRFs (50 computed tomography, 50 magnetic resonance imaging). Each model processed cases with and without constraints to structured outputs.

pmc-13208954.title: Lipidomic Signatures in Feline Disease: A PRISMA-Guided Systematic Review
pmc-13208954.creator: Ana Carolina Fontes, Carolina Santos Silva, Ana Carolina Matos, Isabel Ribeiro Dias, Francisco Peixoto, Maria Manuel Oliveira, Maria Rosario Domingues, Carlos Antunes Viegas
pmc-13208954.description: Background/Objectives: Lipidomics has become a key component of systems biology, enabling comprehensive characterisation of lipid species and their roles in health and disease. As regulators of membrane architecture, energy balance, inflammation, and cellular signalling, lipids offer a powerful framework for understanding metabolic dysfunction. In veterinary medicine, however, lipidomics remains comparatively underdeveloped.

pmc-13277211.title: Genome-wide identification and expression analysis of the bHLH gene family in Lilium davidii var. unicolor and its response to abiotic stress
pmc-13277211.creator: Yue Yang, Mengyue Jing, Yao Qu, Jiaxing Li, Youguo Wang, Tao Yin, Xinyu Yang
pmc-13277211.description: BackgroundBasic helix-loop-helix (bHLH) transcription factors regulate plant growth, stress responses, and hormone signaling. Advances in bioinformatics, the bHLH transcription factor family has been comprehensively identified and characterized across a wide range of organisms. However, a genome-wide analysis of this family has not yet been performed in Lilium davidii var.

pmc-13342740.title: Transforming growth factor alpha polymorphism and cleft lip and palate in North Indian Population
pmc-13342740.creator: Juhi Yadav, Pradeep Raghav, Raj K. Mishra, Divya N. Upadhyaya, Veerendra Prasad, Chandra P. Chaturvedi, Kritanjali Singh
pmc-13342740.description: Introduction:One of the most common congenital malformations, with widespread racial and regional variation, is an orofacial cleft. Cleft lip and palate (CLP) are a congenital anomaly that results in incomplete or non-fusion of the lip and/or palate during the embryonic development of the child.

pmc-13377339.title: Lower Striatal and Cortical Calretinin Interneuron Density Associated With Altered Social Behavior in Cntnap2 Knockout Mice
pmc-13377339.creator: Krisztina Sáfár, Vivien Szendi, Paulina Hoppa, Yutong Wang, Fanni Á. Seres, Szilvia Bartók, Tyler Teadora, Lei Shi, Árpád Dobolyi, Gina Puska, István Adorján
pmc-13377339.description: Variants in the CNTNAP2 gene, encoding the cell adhesion molecule CASPR2, have been identified as genetic risk factors for autism spectrum disorder (ASD). However, the mechanisms through which CNTNAP2 dysfunction alters circuit function remain unknown. Interneurons, as key regulators of excitatory–inhibitory balance, represent a candidate source of vulnerability.

pmc-13394062.title: Interpreting Early‐Onset Colorectal Cancer in Japan: A Descriptive Epidemiologic Review Using Public Summary Statistics
pmc-13394062.creator: Keitaro Matsuo, Hidemi Ito
pmc-13394062.description: Early‐onset colorectal cancer (EOCRC) is increasingly described as a rising disease entity, but the descriptive epidemiologic conditions required to interpret that rise remain incompletely articulated. Using Japanese public summary statistics, we conducted a reproducible descriptive epidemiology review to examine whether the observed EOCRC signal is more compatible with substantial detection‐related effects, a concurrent increase in invasive burden, or both.
